mainTopic: Tearing to sew in the משכן, רב's teachings about stitching, the מגוש and calculating תקופות ומזלות, trapping and cracking a חלזון, and which מלאכה slaughtering falls under
overview: The amud opens by finishing the discussion of tearing in order to sew. In the משכן, a curtain with a worm hole was torn further and then sewn neatly. רב זוטרא בר טוביה then quotes three teachings of רב. Tightening a loose stitch on שבת makes a person חייב חטאת. Learning even one thing from a מגוש makes a person liable for death. A person who can calculate תקופות ומזלות but does not should not be spoken with. The גמרא proves that רב holds a מגוש is a heretic (גדופי), and it brings sources showing that calculating the seasons is praised and is even a מצוה. Next, on trapping, a ברייתא brings a מחלוקת between the רבנן and רבי יהודה about whether cracking a חלזון adds a חיוב of דישה. The גמרא then asks why there is no חיוב for killing the חלזון, and it gives two answers: רבי יוחנן's and רבא's. Finally, רב and שמואל argue about whether a שוחט is liable for צובע or for נטילת נשמה.

steps.title: Where tearing in order to sew happened in the משכן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that tearing in order to sew happened in the משכן: when a worm made a hole in a curtain, they tore the hole bigger and then sewed it up neatly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because when a worm made a hole in a curtain of the משכן, they would tear it more and then sew it.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes an answer that started on the previous עמוד. It shows how קורע על מנת לתפור (tearing in order to sew) happened in the משכן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every מלאכה of שבת needs a model in the work of the משכן. A small worm hole cannot be sewn smoothly, so they first tore it into a longer tear and then sewed it flat. That tearing was done for the sake of sewing, so it counts as a constructive act.

keyTerms.meaning: A curtain or tapestry of the משכן
A worm (moth) that eats holes in cloth

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think they tore just to cause damage. They tore only so that the sewing would come out neat. That purpose is exactly what makes this tearing count as a מלאכה.

phrases.english: For a curtain that a worm got into (and made a hole),
phrases.notes: This is still answering how קורע על מנת לתפור was done in the משכן.

phrases.english: they would tear it and then sew it up.
phrases.notes: They made the tear bigger so the sewn seam would lie flat and neat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer to the question asked on the previous עמוד about how this מלאכה appeared in the משכן.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A curtain damaged by a worm was torn further and then sewn, which is tearing for the purpose of sewing.

steps.title: Tightening a loose stitch on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that someone who pulls a sewing thread tight on שבת is חייב חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זוטרא בר טוביה said in the name of רב: One who pulls tight a sewing thread on שבת is liable to bring a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זוטרא בר טוביה quotes רב: pulling a loose stitch tight on שבת counts as sewing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picture a seam that has started to separate. If you pull the thread so the two pieces join again, you have done what sewing does. So even though you added no new stitch, you are liable for תופר.

keyTerms.meaning: One who stretches or pulls tight
Liable to bring a sin-offering (for doing a מלאכה by accident)

steps.whyThisMatters: In practice, you may not tighten a loose seam on שבת. Doing so counts as the מלאכה of sewing.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב זוּטְרָא בַּר טוֹבִיָּה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Zutra bar Toviya said that Rav said:
One who pulls tight a thread of stitching on Shabbat
is liable to a sin-offering,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב זוּטְרָא בַּר טוֹבִיָּה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another ruling about sewing (תופר), the topic the גמרא was just discussing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pulling a stitch thread tight on שבת counts as sewing and makes a person חייב חטאת.

steps.title: Two more teachings of רב: learning from a מגוש, and calculating the seasons
steps.stepSummary: In the same list, רב says that learning one thing from a מגוש makes a person liable for death. He also says that one who can calculate תקופות ומזלות but does not should not be spoken with.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one who learns even one thing from a מגוש is liable to death. And one who knows how to calculate the seasons and constellations but does not do so, it is forbidden to speak with him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זוטרא continues quoting רב with two teachings that have nothing to do with שבת. The גמרא will explain both of them in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These two rulings are quoted here only because they came in the same list from the same speaker as the stitching rule. The ruling about the מגוש is very strict, and the strictness will matter in step 5. The ruling about calculating seasons treats ignoring God's handiwork as a serious failing.

keyTerms.meaning: Astronomical seasons and the movement of constellations
It is forbidden to speak with him

steps.confusionAlert: These rulings are not about שבת. They are quoted here only because the same רב said them together with the stitching rule.

phrases.english: And one who learns one thing from a magosh
is liable to death,
and one who knows how to calculate seasons and constellations
and does not calculate
it is forbidden to speak with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same list of רב's teachings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Learning from a מגוש makes a person liable for death. A person who is able to calculate the seasons but does not should be shunned.

steps.title: רב and שמואל argue about what a מגוש is
steps.stepSummary: רב and שמואל disagree about what a מגוש is. One says sorcerers (חרשי), and the other says heretics (גדופי).
steps.simpleTranslation: About the אמגושתא, רב and שמואל disagree: one says they are sorcerers, and the other says they are blasphemers or heretics.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a מחלוקת about what a מגוש is. It does not yet say which opinion belongs to רב and which to שמואל, and it is setting up the next step to figure that out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a מגוש is a sorcerer, his danger is magic. If a מגוש is a heretic, his danger is false beliefs about God. Which definition is right decides how serious it is to learn from him.

keyTerms.meaning: The practice or identity of the מגוש
One said (the speaker is not named)

phrases.english: Regarding the magosh — Rav and Shmuel disagree:
one says: sorcerers,
and one says: heretics/blasphemers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the term מגוש from רב's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a מחלוקת whether a מגוש is a sorcerer or a heretic.

steps.title: Proof that רב is the one who says heretics
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves that רב holds that a מגוש is a heretic. רב made learning from a מגוש a capital offense, and simply learning about sorcery is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Conclude that רב is the one who said 'heretics.' רב זוטרא בר טוביה said in the name of רב that one who learns one thing from a מגוש is liable to death. If you think a מגוש is a sorcerer, the Torah wrote 'Do not learn to do,' which means you may learn in order to understand and to teach. So conclude that רב means heretics.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses רב's own ruling from step 3 to show which side of the מחלוקת he holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'לא תלמד לעשות' teach that learning sorcery only in order to understand it, and to rule about it, is allowed. If a מגוש were only a sorcerer, learning from him could not carry a death penalty. Since רב said it does, he must hold that a מגוש is a heretic, and learning heresy is dangerous in itself.

keyTerms.meaning: For if it would enter your mind
Do not learn to do (the practices of the nations)
To understand and to teach or rule

steps.whatToRemember: Learning about sorcery in order to understand it is allowed. Learning from heretics is far more dangerous, and רב holds that a מגוש is a heretic.

phrases.english: Conclude that Rav is the one who said 'heretics,'

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב זוּטְרָא בַּר טוֹבִיָּה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: since Rav Zutra bar Toviya said that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: הַלּוֹמֵד דָּבָר אֶחָד מִן הַמָּגוֹשׁ חַיָּיב מִיתָה.
phrases.english: One who learns one thing from a magosh is liable to death.
For if you think they are sorcerers:
isn't it written: 'You shall not learn to do' —
but you may learn in order to understand and to teach!
Conclude it (that Rav means heretics).
phrases.notes: This one word wraps up the proof.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles which opinion in the מחלוקת of step 4 belongs to רב.
steps.raayaObject: That רב holds a מגוש is a heretic (גדופי).
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's ruling that learning from a מגוש is a capital offense, together with the דרשה on 'לא תלמד לעשות' that allows learning sorcery in order to understand it.

steps.title: A harsh verse about one who ignores the calculation of the seasons
steps.stepSummary: בר קפרא applies a critical verse to someone who can calculate the seasons and constellations but does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן פזי said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי, quoting בר קפרא: Anyone who knows how to calculate the seasons and constellations but does not, the verse says about him: 'They do not notice the work of ה׳, and they do not see His handiwork.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains רב's third teaching, about calculating the seasons. It brings a verse that criticizes a person who does not calculate them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The movements of the heavens are God's own handiwork. A person who could understand them and does not bother is ignoring God's works. This explains why רב said such a person should be shunned.

keyTerms.meaning: They do not look or take notice

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי מִשּׁוּם בַּר קַפָּרָא:
phrases.english: that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said in the name of bar Kappara:
Anyone who knows how to calculate seasons and constellations
and does not calculate,
about him the verse says:
'They do not take notice of the work of ה׳
and they do not see His handiwork.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן פַּזִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי מִשּׁוּם בַּר קַפָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the third ruling of step 3 and gives a verse that criticizes not calculating.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who can calculate the seasons but does not is criticized by the verse for ignoring God's handiwork.

steps.title: Calculating the seasons is a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן derives from a פסוק that there is a מצוה to calculate the seasons and constellations, because this is the wisdom the nations can see.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יוחנן: From where do we know that it is a מצוה for a person to calculate the seasons and constellations? As it says: 'Guard and do them, for it is your wisdom and understanding in the eyes of the nations.' Which wisdom and understanding is in the eyes of the nations? You must say this is the calculation of the seasons and constellations.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן goes one step further than בר קפרא. He shows that calculating the seasons is not just praiseworthy but an actual מצוה, and he brings a source for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of a wisdom of ours that the nations can see and admire. Most Torah wisdom cannot be checked by outsiders. Astronomical calculations, however, can be checked by anyone who looks at the sky, so the פסוק must be pointing to them.

keyTerms.meaning: In the eyes of the nations
You must say, it must be

steps.whatToRemember: There are two levels here. בר קפרא criticizes a person who ignores calculating the seasons. רבי יוחנן makes calculating them a מצוה, based on 'כי היא חכמתכם ובינתכם לעיני העמים'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sugya is a classic source for the value of studying astronomy, especially since the Jewish calendar depends on it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
From where do we know that it is a מצוה upon a person
to calculate seasons and constellations?
As it says: 'And you shall guard and perform,
for it is your wisdom and your understanding
in the eyes of the nations.'
Which wisdom and understanding
is in the eyes of the nations?
You must say:
This is the calculation of seasons and constellations.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִנַּיִן שֶׁמִּצְוָה עַל הָאָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 6 by raising the value of calculating from praiseworthy to a full מצוה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is a מצוה to calculate the seasons and constellations, learned from 'כי היא חכמתכם ובינתכם לעיני העמים'.

steps.title: Trapping and cracking a חלזון: one חיוב or two
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'הצד צבי' and brings a ברייתא. Someone who traps a חלזון and cracks it open is liable once according to the רבנן, and twice according to רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'One who traps a deer, etc.' The Rabbis taught in a ברייתא: One who traps a חלזון and cracks it open is liable only once. רבי יהודה says he is liable twice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next מלאכה in the משנה, which is trapping. It brings a ברייתא with a dispute about trapping a חלזון and then cracking it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that trapping the חלזון is a חיוב of צד. The argument is only about the second act, cracking it open to get its dye. The רבנן say it adds nothing, and רבי יהודה says it is a second, separate חיוב.

keyTerms.meaning: One who traps (the מלאכה of trapping)
A sea creature whose blood was used to make dye (תכלת)
One who cracks or squeezes it open

phrases.english: 'One who traps a deer, etc.'
The Rabbis taught:
One who traps a חלזון and cracks it open,
is liable only once.
רבי יהודה says: he is liable twice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new section begins on the next מלאכה in the משנה, trapping.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The רבנן say trapping and cracking a חלזון is one חיוב. רבי יהודה says it is two.

steps.title: Is cracking included in threshing
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains that רבי יהודה holds cracking is a form of דישה. The רבנן disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה used to say that cracking falls under the category of threshing. They said to him: cracking is not included in threshing.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives the reason behind the dispute. The question is whether cracking open the חלזון counts as דישה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דישה means separating something you want from the covering it sits in, the way grain is separated from its husk. רבי יהודה sees cracking the shell to reach the dye as the same idea. The רבנן deny this, and the next step, where רבא explains their reason, tells us why.

keyTerms.meaning: Threshing, separating a desired item from its covering

phrases.english: For רבי יהודה used to say:
Cracking is included in threshing.
They said to him:
Cracking is not included in threshing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind the dispute in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whether the second חיוב applies depends on whether פציעה counts as דישה.

steps.title: רבא explains why the רבנן say cracking is not threshing
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that according to the רבנן, דישה only applies to things that grow from the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What is the reason of the רבנן? They hold that threshing applies only to things that grow from the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains why the רבנן reject רבי יהודה's view. He asks his own question and answers it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן do not deny that cracking separates the dye from the shell. They limit the category of דישה to plant produce, like grain from the field. A חלזון is a creature and not something that grows from the ground, so cracking it cannot be דישה.

keyTerms.meaning: Things that grow from the ground

phrases.english: Rava said:
What is the reason of the Rabbis?
They hold that there is no threshing
except for things that grow from the ground.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the רבנן's position from step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the רבנן, דישה is limited to גידולי קרקע.

steps.title: Why is he not liable for killing the חלזון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the רבנן's ruling of only one חיוב. Cracking the חלזון should also make him liable for נטילת נשמה, taking a life.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him also be liable for taking a life!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ruling of 'only one חיוב.' Even if cracking is not threshing, cracking the creature kills it, so there should be a second חיוב for killing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge sets דישה aside and points to a different מלאכה, נטילת נשמה. Cracking a living חלזון takes its life, which is a well-known מלאכה. So the count of 'only one' still seems wrong.

phrases.english: But let him also be liable
for taking a life!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the רבנן's ruling of only one חיוב from step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The רבנן's ruling that trapping and cracking a חלזון is only one חיוב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Cracking kills the creature, so there should be a second חיוב of נטילת נשמה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: it was already dead
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the ברייתא is talking about a case where he cracked the חלזון after it was already dead.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: The case is where he cracked it when it was dead.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the challenge by narrowing the case in the ברייתא. The חלזון was already dead when he cracked it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the creature was dead, cracking it takes no life, so there is no נטילת נשמה. That is why the רבנן count only one חיוב, for the trapping.

keyTerms.meaning: He cracked it when it was dead

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
It is where he cracked it when it was dead.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the חלזון was alive when it was cracked.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is talking about a dead חלזון, so no life was taken.

steps.title: רבא: even if alive, he did not mean to kill it
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different answer. Even if the חלזון was alive, the person was not trying to kill it, so he is not liable for נטילת נשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Even if you say he cracked it while it was alive, he is acting without intent with regard to taking a life.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a second answer to the same challenge. He keeps the case where the חלזון was alive and says the killing was not intended.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן changed the facts of the case. רבא keeps the facts and points to the person's intent instead. The person only wanted the dye, not the death of the creature, so the killing is treated as unintended.

keyTerms.meaning: One who acts without intending the prohibited result

phrases.english: Rava said:
Even if you say he cracked it while alive,
he is acting without intent regarding taking a life.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא שֶׁפְּצָעוֹ חַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the קשיא of step 11, different from רבי יוחנן's.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Cracking a living חלזון should be a חיוב of killing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The killing was not intended, so there is no חיוב for נטילת נשמה.

steps.title: Challenge from פסיק רישיה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא from the known rule that even רבי שמעון agrees a person is liable for a result that is certain to happen. Killing the חלזון is certain.
steps.simpleTranslation: But אביי and רבא both said: רבי שמעון agrees in the case of 'cut off its head and will it not die?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's answer. If the death is guaranteed, a person cannot claim he did not intend it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון usually permits an act whose prohibited result was not intended (דבר שאין מתכוין). He agrees, however, that when the result is certain to happen, which is called פסיק רישיה, the person is liable. Cracking a live חלזון certainly kills it, so 'no intent' should not help, and רבא himself said this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Cut off its head and will it not die?', meaning a result that is certain to happen

steps.confusionAlert: The רבא who is challenged here is the same רבא who said the פסיק רישיה rule. The גמרא is pointing out that his answer seems to contradict his own principle.

phrases.english: But didn't Abaye and Rava
both say:
Rabbi Shimon agrees
in a case of 'cut off its head and will it not die'!

steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the killing is unintended
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The death is certain (פסיק רישיה), and even רבי שמעון holds that a person is liable for a certain result.

steps.title: Here he wants it to stay alive
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this case is different. The trapper wants the חלזון to live as long as possible, because that makes the dye clearer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it is different, because the longer it has life in it, the better for him, so that its dye will be clear.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא's answer. The rule of פסיק רישיה does not apply in the same way when the person actually wants the result not to happen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the death is not just unwanted; it works against the person's goal, because a living חלזון gives better dye. Since he prefers that it stay alive, the certain death is not counted against him. רבא's answer therefore stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It is pleasing to him, it is what he wants

steps.whatToRemember: The חלזון discussion ends here. There are two reasons there is no חיוב for killing: רבי יוחנן says it was already dead, and רבא says the killing was unintended and even against his interest.

phrases.english: Here it is different,
for the more life there is in it,
the better it is for him,
so that its dye will be clear.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: A certain death makes him liable even without intent.
steps.terutzMaskana: When he wants the creature to stay alive, the certain death is not held against him.

steps.title: Which מלאכה does a שוחט violate
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes 'and one who slaughters it' from the משנה and asks under which category of מלאכה slaughtering falls.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And one who slaughters it.' One who slaughters is liable for what?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item in the משנה, slaughtering. It asks which category of מלאכה this belongs to, and this sets up the answers in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists slaughtering as a מלאכה, but it does not say what makes it forbidden. The גמרא wants to identify the exact category behind the חיוב.

phrases.english: 'And one who slaughters it.'
One who slaughters is liable because of what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new section on the next מלאכה in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which category of מלאכה makes a שוחט liable

steps.title: רב says dyeing, שמואל says taking a life
steps.stepSummary: רב says a שוחט is liable for צובע, because the blood colors the skin. שמואל says he is liable for נטילת נשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: because of dyeing. And שמואל said: because of taking a life.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two answers to its question. רב and שמואל disagree about which מלאכה applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב focuses on a side effect of slaughtering: the blood stains the animal's skin, which is a kind of צובע. שמואל focuses on the main result, which is ending the animal's life.

phrases.english: Rav said: because of dyeing.
And Shmuel said:
because of taking a life.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָמַר מִשּׁוּם צוֹבֵעַ וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר מִשּׁוּם נְטִילַת נְשָׁמָה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב says צובע. שמואל says נטילת נשמה.
